# Define the tutorial packaging format

## Description

This epic defines the tutorial packaging format: the structure that lets each
tutorial carry its own metadata, pinned images, and validation manifest so that
tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. It is
the shared foundation that the Dashboard tutorial gallery, the curated notebook
tutorials, and the pipeline tutorial all build against.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial package structure covering:
  - Metadata describing the tutorial (title, description, core journey it covers)
  - Pinned container images the tutorial runs on
  - A validation manifest describing how the tutorial is tested
- Define the versioning scheme for tutorial packages so a tutorial can be
  updated and re-tested without a Dashboard release
- Define the validation manifest schema so tutorial correctness can be checked
  against a given platform release in an automated, repeatable way
- Produce a minimal worked example package for a notebook tutorial and a
  minimal worked example package for a pipeline tutorial — small exemplars that
  validate the format and demonstrate both launch paths. These are
  format-validation fixtures only, not full tutorials; the curated tutorial
  content itself is authored separately by the owning teams, so no tutorial
  authoring effort is duplicated here
- Review the format specification with the consuming teams (Dashboard,
  Workbenches, Pipelines) so all consumers commit to one shared schema

## Acceptance Criteria

- The format specification defines metadata, image pinning, and the validation
  manifest such that a tutorial packaged per the format can be versioned and
  validated independently of a Dashboard release
- A notebook tutorial packaged per the format passes the checks declared in its
  validation manifest
- A pipeline tutorial packaged per the format passes the checks declared in its
  validation manifest
- The format specification is reviewed and accepted by the Dashboard,
  Workbenches, and Pipelines teams

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3** (P1): A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images,
  validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable
  independently of Dashboard releases. This epic fully covers HLR-3.
  Epic priority is P0 by inheritance: this epic transitively enables the P0
  HLR-1 (gallery launch) and HLR-2 (curated tutorials) work.

# Tutorial gallery and one-click launch in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a surface where
users browse curated tutorials and launch one into their own project with one
click — opening a workbench with the tutorial notebook, or importing the
tutorial pipeline. This is the product-code work stream of the tutorial gallery
strategy, owned by the Dashboard team.

This epic is verified against the curated tutorial set: its end-to-end launch
acceptance criteria exercise the six curated tutorials covering the core
journeys, so the gallery work completes after the curated notebook tutorials
and the first-pipeline tutorial have been authored and packaged.

## Scope

- A tutorial gallery surface in the Dashboard that lists available tutorials
  and renders their packaged metadata (title, description, journey)
- One-click launch mechanics for notebook tutorials: create a workbench in the
  user's project with the tutorial notebook, using the pinned images declared
  by the tutorial package
- One-click launch mechanics for pipeline tutorials: import the pipeline into
  the project's Data Science Pipelines instance
- Reading tutorial packages in the defined tutorial packaging format
  (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest)
- The gallery is scoped to curated platform tutorials; community/partner
  intake tooling and localization are out of scope for this release

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can open the tutorial gallery from the Dashboard
- The gallery displays tutorial metadata read from packages in the defined
  tutorial packaging format
- Launching a notebook tutorial from the gallery creates a workbench in the
  user's project with the tutorial notebook available in it
- Launching a pipeline tutorial from the gallery imports the pipeline into the
  user's project
- Each of the six curated tutorials covering the core journeys (first
  workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment,
  first RAG app) launches successfully end-to-end from the gallery
- The launch path follows existing Dashboard patterns for creating workbenches
  and importing pipelines (no new private component APIs; Kubernetes
  resources only)

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1** (P0): The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can
  launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook,
  or importing the pipeline). This epic fully covers HLR-1.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9019: Curated getting-started tutorial gallery

The strategy delivers a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: product code
(the gallery and one-click launch mechanics), authored content (six curated
tutorials spanning notebooks and pipelines), and documentation. These are three
architecturally distinct work streams with different owners and review cycles,
so the strategy is decomposed into a multi-epic DAG rather than a single epic.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E001 | Define the tutorial packaging format | Implementation | Workbenches | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E002 | Tutorial gallery and one-click launch in the Dashboard | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E003 | Author five curated notebook tutorials | Implementation | Workbenches | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E004 | Author the first-pipeline tutorial | Implementation | RHOAI Pipelines | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E005 | Document tutorial gallery usage and tutorial contribution | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P1 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9019-E001 Tutorial packaging format] --> E002[RHAISTRAT-9019-E002 Dashboard gallery and launch]
    E001 --> E003[RHAISTRAT-9019-E003 Notebook tutorials]
    E001 --> E004[RHAISTRAT-9019-E004 Pipeline tutorial]
    E001 --> E005[RHAISTRAT-9019-E005 Documentation]
    E003 --> E002
    E004 --> E002
    E002 --> E005
    E003 --> E005
    E004 --> E005
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 13 (build-against artifact) | The Dashboard gallery code builds against the packaging format (metadata schema, pinned images) to render and launch tutorials; the format is an API-like artifact, not a configuration reference. |
| E001 → E003 | Rule 12/13 (framework → consumer) | Notebook tutorials are packaged in the format; authoring them against an undefined schema would force rework and duplicate the schema definition. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 12/13 (framework → consumer) | The pipeline tutorial is packaged in the same format; same reasoning as E003. |
| E003 → E002 | Rule 13 (artifact consumer) | The gallery epic's end-to-end acceptance criteria launch each of the curated notebook tutorials from the gallery, so it consumes the tutorial packages authored by the notebook tutorial epic as data artifacts; without this edge the gallery epic could complete before any curated tutorial exists, leaving its own AC unverifiable. |
| E004 → E002 | Rule 13 (artifact consumer) | Same reasoning as E003 → E002, for the curated first-pipeline tutorial: the gallery's pipeline-import launch path is verified end-to-end against that tutorial package. |
| E001 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | docs-authoring epic blocked by all Implementation epics. |
| E002 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation describes the shipped gallery and launch behavior. |
| E003 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation references the curated tutorial set. |
| E004 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation references the curated tutorial set. |

E003 and E004 run in parallel once the format exists (Rule 14: different
repos/components, no shared artifacts). E002 follows the two tutorial epics:
its acceptance criteria verify the end-to-end launch of all six curated
tutorials, which are the artifacts produced by those epics — a data dependency
that Rule 14's "no shared artifacts" condition does not cover. (Revised per
adversarial review: the original DAG ran E002 in parallel with E003/E004,
allowing the gallery epic to complete before any curated tutorial existed.) No Investigation
epics: the strategy's Open Questions section is empty, and the remaining
unknowns (exact metadata fields, validation tooling details) are implementation
details the owning teams resolve, not genuine unknowns that change which epics
exist.

| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation for gallery usage and tutorial contribution | RHAISTRAT-9019-E005 |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements. HLR-2 is split across two
epics by component/team boundary (notebook tutorials vs. pipeline tutorial),
not by priority.

## Component and Team Mapping Notes

- Owner teams are taken from `.context/architecture-context/` (Dashboard →
  RHOAI Dashboard; Notebooks → Workbenches; Data Science Pipelines → RHOAI
  Pipelines). The strategy has no Impacted Teams table.
- **E001 component mapping (non-obvious):** the packaging format spans both
  Notebooks and Data Science Pipelines tutorials and is consumed by the
  Dashboard. Assigned the single most-relevant canonical component `Notebooks`
  (five of the six tutorials are notebooks; the format's pinned-image concern
  is the workbench images maintained by the same team). The span is noted here
  per the component-name constraint.
- The "first deployment" and "first RAG app" tutorials are placed in the
  notebook tutorials epic (E003): the journeys are notebook-driven and the
  strategy's affected components include no model-serving component.
- E005 uses canonical component `Documentation` with a docs team; the
  Documentation component has no architecture-context file (it is a content
  process, not a code component), so no onboarding chain applies.
- The worked example packages in the format epic are minimal format-validation
  fixtures only; the curated tutorial content is authored in the notebook and
  pipeline tutorial epics, so no tutorial authoring effort is duplicated
  (revision note from adversarial review).

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections:** the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
  Dependencies table, no formal Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no
  Non-Functional Requirements. Decomposition proceeded from the HLRs and
  problem statement; epic acceptance criteria were derived accordingly.
- **Priority inheritance on E001:** HLR-3 is P1, but the packaging format epic
  is P0 by inheritance — it transitively enables both P0 HLRs (HLR-1 and
  HLR-2). If the team intends the format to land after an initial un-packaged
  release, the tutorials and gallery would need rework to retrofit packaging;
  this decomposition assumes format-first to avoid that duplication.
- **Scope trap risk (recurring validation):** HLR-2 requires each tutorial to
  be "tested against the current release" and HLR-3 makes tutorials "testable
  independently of Dashboard releases", which implies re-validation on future
  releases. The strategy does not state where recurring validation executes
  (CI wiring, schedules). Scope is captured as the validation manifest within
  the packaging format plus per-release testing as an acceptance criterion;
  standing automation infrastructure is not scoped to any epic.
- **Out-of-scope boundary respected:** partner/community tutorial intake
  tooling and localization are excluded per the strategy; the contribution
  process is documented only (E005 scope).

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependencies with uncertain timing. All work is
